newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK gold ends shade up on slight physical offtake.
newsitem.headline: HK gold ends shade up on slight physical offtake.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold ended barely higher on Friday compared to New York's previous close after a day of very quiet trade marked only by light sales from Japan and slight physical offtake, bullion dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$348.50/349.00 an ounce against New York's US$348.40/90 close on Thursday.
"We saw light selling from Japan, probably hedging against TOCOM (Tokyo Commodity Exchange)," said one dealer at an international bank.
Strong support was seen at $348 per ounce, dealers said.
Local physical buyers bought gold in afternoon, and there was some shortcovering which helped gold prices inch up, dealers said.
The move upwards was aided by light European buying when markets there opened, dealers said.
"There is no strong direction at all," said another bullion dealer, noting that gold had traded in a 75 U.S. cent-range.
Local gold ended unchanged at HK$3,226 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained unchanged at nil.
Hong Kong close - US$348.50/349.00 New York close - US$348.40/90
